title: The baptism (Matthew 3:13–17)
hookLine: Jesus steps into the line of sinners, the sky opens, a voice says beloved

lines: A LINE OF PEOPLE WITH REGRETS.
cards: A long line at the river. Everyone in it is there for the same reason: they've done things they regret, and they want to turn around. A tax man.
A soldier. A woman who hasn't spoken to her sister in years. Nobody in that line is showing off.
Then a carpenter from Nazareth steps in and waits his turn like everybody else. When he reaches the front, John looks at him and stops. He knows who this is, and he tries to refuse.

teach.b: John's words, in the Douay-Rheims: "I ought to be baptized by thee, and comest thou to me?" It's backward, he means: you should be baptizing me.
Jesus answers that it is fitting, for now, to fulfill all justice, and John lets him come down into the river. Why get in line at all? Christians have asked that for two thousand years.
The Church's answer: not for his own sins.
He was standing where sinners stand, on purpose, in the water with them. Then the story opens up.

As he comes out, Matthew says, the heavens were opened, and he saw the Spirit of God coming down like a dove and resting on him. And a voice from heaven: "This is my beloved Son, in whom I am well pleased."
Before a single miracle, sermon, follower or healing, he's already beloved. The Church reads the scene as a window onto the Trinity: the Son in the water, the Spirit like a dove, the Father's voice.
The feast of the Baptism of the Lord closes the Christmas season, and it's the first of the Luminous Mysteries of the rosary.
Catholics hear their own baptism in it too: the Catechism teaches that baptism makes a person an adopted child of God.

teach.h: HOLY WATER AT THE CHURCH DOOR.
teach.b: That's why there's holy water at the church door.
People dip their fingers and make the sign of the cross on the way in, remembering the water they came through.

how: Catholics celebrate the Baptism of the Lord as the feast that ends the Christmas season, pray it as the first Luminous Mystery of the rosary, and bless themselves with holy water on entering a church as a reminder of their own baptism.

o: a lifelong vow made to serve as a priest
washing in water: a new start with God
a party held to give a newborn its name

games.q: you're John. the one you've been announcing is standing in your line, waiting to be baptized. what do you do?
o: baptize him quickly, like everyone else.
tell him he should be baptizing you.
announce him to the crowd and step aside.
games.why: John protests: "I ought to be baptized by thee." Jesus says it is fitting for now, and John lets him come.

practice: If you can, touch a little water from a glass or a tap, and feel how cool or warm it is; a Catholic might make the sign of the cross, as at the church door; if not, just let the water be water.
Then sit, and let one sentence rest on you: loved, before doing anything.

wordCard.voice: The baptism. Jesus steps into the river with sinners, and a voice from heaven calls him beloved.

orig.note: Greek: beloved, dearly loved. From agapē, love. The word the voice from heaven uses.

carryVoice: Your line: you are the beloved. Loved first, before any of the day's work. Until tomorrow.
